title: Langley Home Energy Rebates 2026: Township and City of Langley
desc: Rebates for Langley homeowners in 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, split by the Township of Langley and the City of Langley, which have very different housing.
badge: Heat pumps up to $4,000 from BC Hydro
lead: Langley is two municipalities, and the Census treats them as two very different places: the Township has 82% owners and 48% detached houses, while the City is 21% detached and 63% owners.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Langley in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: The Township counted 46,925 households in 2021. 82% own, the highest ownership share of the 18 BC cities we cover. About 48% live in detached houses and 23% in homes built before 1981, the lowest pre-1981 share in this group. Still, 6,640 owner-occupied detached houses date from before 1981. A Township homeowner with an electric-heated house can claim BC Hydro's full set of home rebates. A lot with no gas line may heat with propane or oil, which are outside BC Hydro's program.

The City counted 12,600 households. 38% live in homes built before 1981, and 21% live in detached houses. 63% own. Only 1,765 are owner-occupied detached houses from before 1981, which is a small pool next to the Township, and major repairs were reported by 5.3% of households against 4.1% in the Township. Most City households do not live in a detached house, so check whether your building is covered by the house rebates or the condo program.

The rebate amounts are the same on both sides of the boundary, because BC Hydro and CleanBC are provincial. What differs is the type of home. A Township acreage on a well and propane heat needs a different plan from a City of Langley townhouse on baseboards. Say which you have when you talk to an installer so the quote covers the right equipment.
The January average low is 0.3°C and the 2015 to 2024 record low was -16.8°C. A cold-climate heat pump on BC Hydro's list handles that. Solar gets about 3.33 peak sun hours a day.
installers_intro: These are the best-reviewed heat pump and heating companies in Langley on Google, weighted by review count. Nobody pays to be listed or to rank higher.
claim_steps: Decide whether you are in the Township or the City, and what heats your home.
If it is electric, get HPCN heat pump quotes.
If it is propane or oil, check CleanBC's income limits.
Ask about insulation and windows for pre-1981 homes.
Apply within six months of each invoice.
faq: Are Township and City of Langley rebates different?
No, the programs are provincial. The housing is different.
The Township has more in total (6,640 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981), but the City has a higher share of older homes overall (38% against 23%).
I have a propane acreage in the Township. What applies?
BC Hydro will not pay to replace propane heat. CleanBC pays $3,500, $7,000 or $13,000 by income level.
Do I need an HPCN installer?
For BC Hydro heat pump, insulation and solar rebates, yes.
